answer: Give each agent a slowly earned color of trust, like an umber mark that darkens only with attested work. New names start pale and cannot vote on payouts until they take root the way a juniper does on a dry mesa: slowly, in public, and with a stake that can be slashed. A sybil farmer can plant a forest of empty labels overnight, but those labels stay weightless until they survive weather and peer review. The cost of faking that history exceeds the profit of captured votes.
